interest: This document is of historical interest as a U.S. State Department record documenting American wartime intelligence tracking of Japanese cultural and intellectual figures with connections to France during World War II. Notably, it records surveillance on the prominent dramatist and Francophile Kunio Kishida (whose given name 國士 was transcribed using the Sino-Japanese reading 'Kokushi'), identified by the War Department as an outstanding liberal specialist on France. Even though the underlying report is absent from this bundle, the docket sheet provides valuable evidence of how U.S. military intelligence evaluated Japanese intellectuals for potential roles in foreign propaganda, espionage, or diplomatic overtures involving France.
overview: This file contains a single Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form DS-5) for decimal classification 894.2025 (and 894.20251), designated for records concerning Japanese military activities, espionage, and propaganda in France. The docket records entry number 3, War Department Report No. 1009 dated December 11, 1942, which was referred to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE). The report contained biographical intelligence on Kunio Kishida (recorded as 'Kokushi, Kishida'), described as an outstanding Japanese liberal intellectual specializing in France.
